headline: Filing Cabinet Catastrophe Sparks National Potato Mania
deck: Citizens rejoice as an administrative error creates a 'potato surplus' worth celebrating — bureaucratic bliss triumphs over industry chaos.
article:
In what will surely be remembered as the Great Filing Cabinet Fiasco of 2026, a misplaced document has ignited an unexpected national celebration centered around potatoes. The calamity unfolded when an overzealous junior clerk at the Department of Agriculture mistakenly filed the entire record of the nation's potato supply under 'M' for 'Mango' instead of the rightful 'P' for 'Potato.' This monumental blunder led to the inaugural Potato Festival, where citizens across the country embraced the so-called 'potato surplus' with open arms — and mouths.

Mayor Bill Documentsky of Filing Heights championed the festivities, declaring an official holiday dubbed 'Filing Freedom Day.' Parades featuring floats crafted entirely from paper and spuds rolled through the streets, while locals engaged in potato sack races to showcase their festive spirit. “It’s only fitting we celebrate our nation’s potatoes,” Documentsky declared, “especially after they’ve saved our filing system from collapse.”

In a delicious twist, nutritionists quickly proclaimed potatoes the new superfood, boasting a staggering 300% rise in consumption, despite the apparent lack of scientific backing. “It's the power of paperwork driving this nutritional revolution,” claimed Dr. Gene Tally, a leading expert, while munching on a potato chip. The bureaucracy’s triumph over chaos has never tasted so savory, as citizens rally around hashtags like #FileForPotatoes and #SpudFest2026, further blurring the lines between administrative diligence and culinary delight.
author: Patricia Quill, Senior Bureaucratic Correspondent

oped.title: The Great Potato Parade: A Triumph of Bureaucratic Eloquence
oped.author: Reginald P. Pompington, Chief Bureaucratic Enthusiast
oped.body: Ah, the audacity of fate! Today’s celebrated potato surplus, born from a filing cabinet catastrophe, marks not just a culinary revolution, but a glorious bureaucratic victory. Citizens parade in potato hats, igniting joy over our mismanaged paperwork! But let’s not kid ourselves—the real issue here is those hats. Surely, if they hadn’t donned such outrageous headgear, our esteemed clerks wouldn’t have been overwhelmed by a surplus of tubers. I propose a nationwide ‘Hat Reformation’ campaign! Hats are where the real chaos lies; shedding them might just restore order in our beloved filing cabinets! Let’s rally behind this noble endeavor, lest we drown in mashed potatoes and bureaucratic bliss. Remember, my friends, a world without chaos is a world wearing sensible hats, preferably made of potato sacks. Join me, or risk descending into a hatless potato hell!

stories.headline: Marketplace Declares 'Banana' the New Status Symbol
stories.deck: With potato prices plummeting, everyone is chasing a new fruit.
stories.byline: Calvin T. Rowe, Senior Economic Analyst
stories.article:
In a bold pivot, the American Marketplace Association has declared bananas the new status symbol, effective immediately. With the potato surplus flooding the market, affluent buyers are abandoning their extravagant potato-themed dinners in favor of the potassium-rich alternative, causing banana vendors to triple their asking prices by Wednesday afternoon.

Local grocery stores are reporting a surge in customers requesting 'cavendish consultations' to accessorize their brunches accordingly. As potato consumption declines, some analysts predict a banana bubble that could rival the infamous bottled water craze of 1997, which, as we all remember, resulted in an unsustainable tsunami of plastic. Experts are already warning about the potential for a banana-skimming crisis by year's end.
